thread:
maya: heads up — saw a suspicious cross-account read today. /api/v1/projects?owner_id=org:123 returned project list for org:999 in the same response. logs attached below. :eyes:

maya: repro snippet: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer svc_ABC123" "https://api.redwood.dev/api/v1/projects?owner_id=org:123"` -> returned 4 projects, two of which belong to org:999.

maya: log excerpt: `auth:allow claim(owner_id)=org:123, claim(claimant)=, policy=project.read -> matched policy_id=project_default v2 -> effective_owner=org:999`

sam: who changed the claimant/owner resolution recently? any PRs touching auth resolver?

kevin: @sam yes — I merged a refactor last week to unify owner lookup across API and console (PR #3345). The old code rejected empty claimant and returned 403; new path falls back to the first bound org for the service account. :grimacing:

sam: ugh. can you paste the exact commit? need to know condition that triggers fallback.

kevin: commit 9b3f7a8 — function `resolve_owner_from_claims` now does `return claims.owner || default_owner_for_service_account(sa_id)` rather than `if (!claims.owner) throw Unauthorized`. So if claimant empty, we pick default. Edge-case when default_owner mapping is stale.

maya: observed this with a customer service account that lost its owner claim due to a migration. Should escalate — cross-org reads are high risk.

lia: setting severity P1. @ops-bot can you pin the incident channel and start audit collection?

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-042, collection started, trace-id=trc-52a7. All requests from svc_ABC123 since 2160000000 are being captured.

sam: short-term mitigation: revoke svc_ABC123 token and add inline deny for `project.read` on that principal. kevin: can you roll a hotfix to restore reject-on-empty-claimant?

kevin: working on a two-part fix: (1) policy change to deny when claimant empty and owner specified, (2) patch to rollback fallback behavior. Will open PR and request expedited review.

maya: mitigation done: revoked token, added deny policy in policy-store (policy-id tmp-deny-334). Confirmed no further cross-org reads after 2160001450.

lia: next steps: 1) Full audit of service accounts lacking owner claim (query provided below). 2) Backfill owner_claim from canonical mapping where safe. 3) Patch and canary deploy with extra logging. 4) Run customer notify playbook for affected orgs.

sam: query to find affected principals: `SELECT sa_id FROM service_accounts WHERE owner_claim IS NULL AND last_active > to_timestamp(2160000000);`

kevin: PR opened: #3358 — adds guard + tests. will request security review.

lia: also check KMS access logs; if any cross-org decrypts happened, rotate keys for affected orgs. @kevin please coordinate with cloud-ops.

kevin: pinged cloud-ops, putting key-rotate runbook on my todo.

maya: note for postmortem: root cause = owner-resolution fallback + migration gap. Mitigation = deny + revoke + backfill.

sam: assign owners: kevin=patch+deploy, maya=audit+customer notify, lia=postmortem+comms. Updated incident doc.

lia: tagging: :fire: P1 -> security leadership notified. Will schedule on-call rotation for next 24h to monitor logs.

maya: thanks — I captured sample request IDs for legal forensics: req-987a, req-99ff. saving to incident doc.

sam: good catch, team. When patch lands, let's add an e2e test that simulates empty claimant and asserts 403.

kevin: agreed — adding test and a policy-level unit test. targeting hotfix deploy in next 90m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
